text:
Escalating to human: needs an approach decision before implementation.

The bead's goal — secondary baseline with all pkix-path crypto features — is straightforward, but the *how* has tradeoffs that warrant explicit direction:

**Option A: Reconfigure pkix-difftest deps as feature-gated**

Change `pkix-difftest/Cargo.toml`:
```
pkix-path = { workspace = true, default-features = false, features = ["rsa", "p256"] }

[features]
all-crypto = ["pkix-path/p384", ...]  # whatever exists
```

Then `cargo run -p pkix-difftest --features all-crypto -- run limbo ...`.

Pros: minimal new code, same binary. Cons: muddles the harness's "what does default consumer get?" framing — readers of Cargo.toml see two different feature sets.

**Option B: Sibling cargo target**

Add `pkix-difftest-allfeatures` as a second crate (or a [[bin]] target) that depends on pkix-path with all features. Outputs to `baseline-limbo-allfeatures.{json,md}`.

Pros: framing stays clean, side-by-side comparison is obvious. Cons: doubles the cargo target list, second binary copy.

**Option C: Just document the limitation, don't auto-run**

The 4 online::* + handful of webpki:: ECC cases are now documented in baseline-limbo-analysis.md. Manual reproduction of the all-features run is one Cargo.toml line edit + one cargo invocation. Don't ship a permanent second baseline; document it as an on-demand investigative tool.

Pros: zero new code, low maintenance. Cons: no committed baseline-allfeatures.json to git-diff against on regressions.

Recommend: Option C unless the project plans to grow many crypto-feature variants. Option A if a single auxiliary baseline is enough. Option B only if there will be N≥3 variants worth committing.

Filed by do-beads loop. Same workspace AGENTS.md rule about planning before code.
